elements.element: Customer is not subject to any employee or personnel non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: The operative language binds Customer because it provides that “Neither party shall” solicit covered personnel.

elements.element: Customer is subject to the non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: “Neither party shall” applies the restriction to Customer.

elements.element: The other party is subject to the same non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: “Neither party shall” applies the restriction reciprocally to both parties.

elements.element: The restriction is limited to personnel directly involved with the Services.
elements.evidence: The clause covers only personnel “who have had direct involvement with the Services.”

elements.element: The restriction lasts for twelve months from the end of each covered person’s involvement with the Services.
elements.evidence: The restriction applies “for twelve (12) months after the end of such personnel's involvement with the Services.”

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
Unsolicited approaches by covered personnel are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: The exception expressly covers “unsolicited approaches by such personnel.”

elements.element: The clause does not prohibit hiring personnel where no prohibited solicitation occurred.
elements.evidence: The operative prohibition is limited to “solicit[ing] for hire”; it does not independently prohibit hiring.

result.reason: The clause fully reaches the fallback but not the preferred position because it continues to bind Customer. It is not strictly minimal because the new exception also covers “other general solicitations not specifically targeted,” which is broader than the requested general-advertisement carve-out. The drafting otherwise preserves the solicitation-only structure and unrelated terms, although the forward reference to “such personnel” slightly reduces clarity.
